newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees foreign investment lower in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees foreign investment lower in 1997.

text.p: Indonesia's Investment Minister Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo on Thursday predicted foreign investment approved by the government would be lower in the 1997 calendar year from the 1996 figure of $29.9 billion.
"I think foreign investment will be lower in 1997, compared with that in 1996," Sanyoto told reporters.
"I don't know exactly what is the reason. I am still studying it. But our investment rules seem to be no problem," he said.
Sanyoto said earlier this month Indonesia had approved foreign investment proposals amounting to $14.4 billion in the first five months of the year, a drop of 25.5 percent from the year-ago period.
He said the drop was due to the country's general elections, held last month, and was not a major concern.
The 1996 approved foreign investment figure was already down from $39.9 billion in 1995.
